cohort: The study included full-term pregnant women in their third trimester, comparing those diagnosed with SARS-CoV-2 infection to uninfected controls.
finding: SARS-CoV-2 infection in late pregnancy was associated with significant alterations in maternal serum proteomics and metabolomics, as well as a higher incidence of cesarean section, postpartum reproductive tract infection, and fetal distress.
mod_finding: The incidence of cesarean section was significantly higher in the COVID-19 group compared to the control group.
cross-section timing: Late pregnancy (third trimester), with serum samples collected one week before delivery for controls and within two days after fever onset for the COVID-19 group.
